title: Drive — A quiet man behind the wheel

hook.context: Ismi aytilmagan qahramon o'z ishini shunday qisqa ta'riflaydi: men faqat haydayman — boshqa ishlarga aralashmayman. Ikki so'zli gap — Present Simple: doimiy kasb va odat.

reading: The main character never tells anyone his name. During the day he works as a stunt driver for films and as a mechanic in a small garage in Los Angeles.

At night he has a secret job: he drives the getaway car for criminals. He is such a good driver that the police can never catch him. He gives his clients exactly five minutes, and he never carries a gun.
He is so quiet that people sometimes think he is cold. In fact, he is just shy and very careful with words.
One day he meets his neighbour Irene and her little son, Benicio. Irene is kind and lonely, and the Driver starts to spend time with them.
Irene's husband, Standard, comes home from prison. He owes money to dangerous people, and he isn't strong enough to protect his family alone.
The Driver decides to help him with one last job. But the job is too dangerous, and everything goes wrong.
To keep Irene and Benicio safe, the Driver has to face the criminals himself. He understands that you can't stay quiet forever when the people you love are in danger.

grammar.title: too / enough, so / such
explain: **too + sifat** — me'yordan ortiq (salbiy): The job is **too dangerous**. **too ... to do**: It's too cold **to swim**.
**sifat + enough** — yetarli; **enough** sifatdan KEYIN, otdan OLDIN keladi: He isn't **strong enough**. We have **enough money**.
**so + sifat** (artiklsiz): He is **so quiet** that people think he is cold. **such + (a/an) + sifat + ot**: He is **such a good driver** that the police can't catch him.
Ko'plik va sanalmaydigan otlarda such artiklsiz: **such** beautiful eyes, **such** bad weather.
